title: B06 midpoint IV recovery: archived experiment and findings evidence
scope: Documentation of a completed in-memory empirical run; no production/dashboard mutation.

protocol.name: B06 midpoint IV recovery diagnostic
protocol.scope: Same fifty sampled days, 374 parents, eleven sectors; no new observations, no file mutations. Previously examined sample: exploratory sensitivity study, not out-of-sample validation.
protocol.score: +5 SPX points before -15 within original 60 minutes; no post-target assessment.

variants.original: Existing positive finite ordered bid/mid/ask IV and quote rules; reproduce saved ATM measures and original classifications.
variants.midpoint: Drop only bid-IV validity and bid-IV<=mid-IV checks. Keep strictly positive finite bid quote, midpoint and ask, ordered quotes, positive finite midpoint/ask IV with midpoint IV<=ask IV; original endpoint identity, underlying age0..60 seconds, expiry8..65DTE.
variants.guarded_100: Use midpoint-selected strikes/expirations; reject the whole ATM minute if any selected quote has spread/midpoint>1.00 or lacks positive ordered quote at the immediately preceding native minute or shows bid<0.5*previous_bid while ask>=0.9*previous_ask OR ask>2*previous_ask while bid<=1.1*previous_bid. Never search for farther strikes to evade these guards.
variants.guarded_50: Same as guarded_100 except spread/midpoint<=0.50; predeclared sensitivity only.

protocol.primary: guarded_100 is the primary candidate. No threshold search or promotion based on greatest observed hit rate.
protocol.measurement: Identical log-strike variance interpolation, calendar30-day total variance interpolation and average call/put variance. All30 minutes T-35..T-6 required. Negative second-half slope and negative change in slope; six of eleven, missing-sector bounds yes/no/unknown unchanged. Invalid bid IV yields no invented bid-side uncertainty bound.
protocol.quality_evaluation: Recoverable sector-minute and sector/event windows, previously valid observations lost/changed, same-contract preceding/following-minute diagnostics for audit only, unchanged quoted prices, source width and shock. No lookahead in admissibility.
protocol.outcome_evaluation: All four variants' broad falling and accelerating groups, target/adverse/neither, retained/added/lost entries and successful targets, active days, frozen original-membership matched cohorts, paired whole-date 10000-draw bootstrap seed20260919 across all50days. No independent-entry assumptions; no reoptimization.
protocol.validation: Original ATM baseline reproduced from raw data; original239/51/84 baseline and93/67 selected. Synthetic guard boundary tests, missing-prior handling, no fallback and causal invariance; check original source hashes before/after.

import hashlib,importlib.util,json,time
from pathlib import Path
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor,as_completed
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
ROOT=Path('/Users/dgrissen/Dev/delta_bomb/outputs/b06_sector_surface_50d_2026-09-13')
VARIANTS=['original','midpoint','guarded_100','guarded_50']
SYMS=['XLC','XLY','XLP','XLE','XLF','XLV','XLI','XLB','XLRE','XLK','XLU']
EPS=1e-12
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('frozen_surface',ROOT/'surface.py')
surf=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(surf)
def digest(path):return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
def safe(x):
 if isinstance(x,dict):return {str(k):safe(v) for k,v in x.items()}
 if isinstance(x,(list,tuple)):return [safe(v) for v in x]
 if isinstance(x,np.ndarray):return safe(x.tolist())
 if isinstance(x,(np.integer,np.bool_)):return x.item()
 if isinstance(x,(float,np.floating)):return float(x) if np.isfinite(x) else None
 return x
def emit(tag,x):print(tag,json.dumps(safe(x),allow_nan=False),flush=True)
def add_quality(p):
 p=p.sort_values(['expiration','right','strike','timestamp']).reset_index(drop=True).copy()
 p['row_id']=np.arange(len(p))
 g=p.groupby(['expiration','right','strike'],sort=False)
 pb,pa,pt=g.bid.shift(1),g.ask.shift(1),g.timestamp.shift(1)
 prev=((p.timestamp-pt).dt.total_seconds().eq(60)&np.isfinite(pb)&np.isfinite(pa)&pb.gt(0)&pa.ge(pb))
 p['previous_ok']=prev
 p['quote_shock']=prev&(((p.bid<.5*pb)&(p.ask>=.9*pa))|((p.ask>2*pa)&(p.bid<=1.1*pb)))
 p['width']=(p.ask-p.bid)/p.midpoint
 p['price_update']=prev&(p.bid.ne(pb)|p.ask.ne(pa))
 oldv=p.valid.to_numpy()
 fields=['strike','bid','midpoint','ask','underlying_price','implied_vol','ask_implied_vol']
 p['mid_valid']=(np.isfinite(p[fields])&p[fields].gt(0)).all(axis=1)&p.endpoint_match&p.bid.le(p.midpoint)&p.midpoint.le(p.ask)&p.implied_vol.le(p.ask_implied_vol)&p.reported_underlying_age_seconds.between(0,60)&p.dte.between(8,65)&p.right.isin(['C','P'])
 assert (~oldv|p.mid_valid.to_numpy()).all()
 p['x']=np.log(p.strike/p.underlying_price)
 pv,nv,nt=g.implied_vol.shift(1),g.implied_vol.shift(-1),g.timestamp.shift(-1)
 neighbors=(p.timestamp-pt).dt.total_seconds().eq(60)&(nt-p.timestamp).dt.total_seconds().eq(60)&np.isfinite(pv)&np.isfinite(nv)&pv.gt(0)&nv.gt(0)
 p['neighbor_deviation']=np.where(neighbors,100*(p.implied_vol-(pv+nv)/2).abs(),np.nan)
 p['unchanged_quotes']=prev&p.bid.eq(pb)&p.ask.eq(pa)
 p['iv_changed']=prev&p.implied_vol.ne(pv)
 return p
def make_surface(p,valid_col,grid):
 q=p[p[valid_col]].copy()
 keys=['timestamp','right','dte']
 low=q[q.x.le(0)].sort_values('x',kind='stable').groupby(keys,sort=False).tail(1)
 high=q[q.x.ge(0)].sort_values('x',kind='stable').groupby(keys,sort=False).head(1)
 f=['underlying_price','underlying_timestamp','x','implied_vol','width','previous_ok','quote_shock','price_update','row_id']
 pairs=low[keys+f].merge(high[keys+f],on=keys,suffixes=('_lo','_hi'),validate='one_to_one')
 pairs=pairs[pairs.underlying_price_lo.eq(pairs.underlying_price_hi)&pairs.underlying_timestamp_lo.eq(pairs.underlying_timestamp_hi)].copy()
 gap=(pairs.x_hi-pairs.x_lo).to_numpy()
 weight=np.divide(pairs.x_hi.to_numpy(),gap,out=np.ones(len(pairs)),where=gap!=0)
 pairs['variance']=weight*pairs.implied_vol_lo**2+(1-weight)*pairs.implied_vol_hi**2
 pairs['max_width']=pairs[['width_lo','width_hi']].max(axis=1)
 pairs['prior_ok']=pairs.previous_ok_lo & pairs.previous_ok_hi
 pairs['shock']=pairs.quote_shock_lo | pairs.quote_shock_hi
 pairs['updated']=pairs.price_update_lo | pairs.price_update_hi
 tenors=np.sort(p.loc[p.dte.between(8,65),'dte'].unique())
 if 30 in tenors:tenors=np.array([30]);weights=np.array([1.])
 else:
  lower=tenors[tenors<30];upper=tenors[tenors>30]
  assert len(lower) and len(upper)
  tenors=np.array([lower[-1],upper[0]])
  weights=np.array([tenors[1]-30,30-tenors[0]])/(tenors[1]-tenors[0])
 arr=pd.DataFrame(index=grid)
 variances=[];widths=[];prior=[];shocks=[];updates=[];spots=[];utimes=[]
 for dte,w in zip(tenors,weights):
  for right in ['C','P']:
   z=pairs[pairs.dte.eq(dte)&pairs.right.eq(right)].set_index('timestamp').reindex(grid)
   variances.append(w*dte/30*z.variance/2)
   widths.append(z.max_width)
   prior.append(z.prior_ok.fillna(False).astype(bool))
   shocks.append(z.shock.fillna(True).astype(bool))
   updates.append(z.updated.fillna(False).astype(bool))
   spots.append(z.underlying_price_lo);utimes.append(z.underlying_timestamp_lo)
 all_variances=pd.concat(variances,axis=1)
 valid=all_variances.notna().all(axis=1)
 spot=pd.concat(spots,axis=1);uts=pd.concat(utimes,axis=1)
 valid &= spot.eq(spot.iloc[:,0],axis=0).all(axis=1)&uts.eq(uts.iloc[:,0],axis=0).all(axis=1)
 arr['iv']=100*np.sqrt(all_variances.sum(axis=1)).where(valid)
 arr['max_width']=pd.concat(widths,axis=1).max(axis=1)
 arr['prior_ok']=pd.concat(prior,axis=1).all(axis=1)
 arr['shock']=pd.concat(shocks,axis=1).any(axis=1)
 arr['updated']=pd.concat(updates,axis=1).any(axis=1)
 arr['guard100']=valid&arr.max_width.le(1.)&arr.prior_ok&~arr.shock
 arr['guard50']=valid&arr.max_width.le(.5)&arr.prior_ok&~arr.shock
 return arr,pairs
def guard_tests():
 def ok(bid,ask,pbid,pask,cap=1,known=True):
  mid=(bid+ask)/2
  shock=(bid<.5*pbid and ask>=.9*pask) or (ask>2*pask and bid<=1.1*pbid)
  return bid>0 and ask>=bid and known and (ask-bid)/mid<=cap and not shock
 assert ok(.6,1.15,.6,1.15)
 assert not ok(.6,1.15,.6,1.15,.5)
 assert not ok(.01,1.63,1.11,1.51)
 assert not ok(.65,2.8,.65,.8)
 assert ok(.6,.8,1.2,1.6)
 assert not ok(0,.8,.6,.8)
 assert not ok(.6,.8,.6,.8,known=False)
 assert ok(.5,1.5,.5,1.5)
 assert not ok(.5,1.50001,.5,1.50001)
 assert not ok(.49,1.1,1.,1.1)
 return 10
dates=pd.read_csv(ROOT/'selected_days.csv').date.tolist()
parents=pd.read_csv(ROOT/'b06_parents.csv')
assert len(dates)==50 and len(parents)==374
byday={d:f for d,f in parents.groupby('date')}
metadata=[ROOT/'surfaces'/f'{d}_{s}.json' for d in dates for s in SYMS]
jobs=[json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in metadata if p.exists()]
assert len(jobs)==537
input_hashes={}
for job in jobs:input_hashes.update(job['signature']['inputs'])
control_paths=[ROOT/f for f in ['surface.py','breadth.py','b06_parents.csv','selected_days.csv','basket_event_features.csv','sector_event_features.csv','event_paths.csv']]
control_hashes={str(p):digest(p) for p in control_paths}
assert digest(ROOT/'surface.py')==jobs[0]['signature']['code_sha256']
started=time.monotonic()
emit('PRE_OUTCOME_PROTOCOL',PROTOCOL)
emit('PROTOCOL_SHA256',hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(PROTOCOL,sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest())
emit('GUARD_TESTS',{'passed':guard_tests()})
def process(job):
 day,sym=job['date'],job['symbol'];iv=[];greeks=[]
 for path,sha in job['signature']['inputs'].items():
  assert digest(path)==sha,path
  d=pd.read_parquet(path)
  (iv if 'implied_volatility' in path else greeks).append(d)
 prepared=surf._prepare(pd.concat(iv,ignore_index=True),pd.concat(greeks,ignore_index=True))
 p=add_quality(prepared)
 old=pd.read_parquet(job['path']).set_index('timestamp')
 grid=old.index
 assert len(grid)==300 and not grid.has_duplicates
 original,opairs=make_surface(p,'valid',grid)
 relaxed,rpairs=make_surface(p,'mid_valid',grid)
 np.testing.assert_allclose(original.iv.to_numpy(),old.atm.to_numpy(),rtol=0,atol=1e-10,equal_nan=True)
 series={'original':original.iv,'midpoint':relaxed.iv,'guarded_100':relaxed.iv.where(relaxed.guard100),'guarded_50':relaxed.iv.where(relaxed.guard50)}
 s_gaps=old.atm_call_status.eq('no_strike_bracket')|old.atm_put_status.eq('no_strike_bracket')
 coverage=[];quality=[];features=[]
 for variant,values in series.items():
  avail=values.notna();oldavail=old.atm.notna()
  coverage.append({'date':day,'symbol':sym,'variant':variant,'valid_minutes':int(avail.sum()),'recovered_minutes':int((avail&~oldavail).sum()),'recovered_S_minutes':int((avail&s_gaps).sum()),'lost_original_minutes':int((~avail&oldavail).sum()),'changed_original_minutes':int((avail&oldavail&(values-old.atm).abs().gt(1e-8)).sum())})
  pairs=opairs if variant=='original' else rpairs
  used=pairs[pairs.timestamp.isin(grid[avail])]
  ids=np.unique(np.r_[used.row_id_lo.to_numpy(dtype=int),used.row_id_hi.to_numpy(dtype=int)])
  nodes=p.iloc[ids]
  deviations=nodes.neighbor_deviation.dropna().to_numpy()
  quality.append({'variant':variant,'n':len(nodes),'missing_bid_iv_nodes':int((~nodes.valid).sum()),'with_neighbors':len(deviations),'neighbor_over1':int((deviations>1).sum()),'neighbor_over5':int((deviations>5).sum()),'prior_ok':int(nodes.previous_ok.sum()),'unchanged':int(nodes.unchanged_quotes.sum()),'unchanged_iv_moves':int((nodes.unchanged_quotes&nodes.iv_changed).sum()),'deviations':deviations,'widths':nodes.width.to_numpy()})
  for event in byday.get(day,pd.DataFrame()).itertuples():
   ix=np.arange(int(event.parent_min)-35-570,int(event.parent_min)-5-570)
   assert len(ix)==30 and ix.min()>=0 and ix.max()<300
   window=values.iloc[ix].to_numpy()
   available=bool(np.isfinite(window).all())
   b1=b2=a=np.nan
   if available:
    weights=np.arange(15)-7
    b1=float(np.dot(weights,window[:15])/280)
    b2=float(np.dot(weights,window[15:])/280)
    a=(b2-b1)/15
   update_frame=original if variant=='original' else relaxed
   updates=update_frame.updated.iloc[ix].to_numpy()
   features.append({'date':day,'episode_id':event.episode_id,'parent_min':int(event.parent_min),'symbol':sym,'variant':variant,'available':available,'samples':int(np.isfinite(window).sum()),'b1':b1,'b2':b2,'acceleration':a,'falling':bool(available and b2<-EPS),'accelerating':bool(available and b2<-EPS and a<-EPS),'quote_change_both_halves':bool(available and updates[:15].any() and updates[15:].any())})
 causal=None
 if (day,sym) in [('2026-01-06','XLRE'),('2026-01-28','XLF')]:
  cut=pd.Timestamp(day+' 10:15',tz='America/New_York') if sym=='XLRE' else pd.Timestamp(day+' 14:01',tz='America/New_York')
  prefix=add_quality(prepared[prepared.timestamp.le(cut)])
  gp=grid[grid<=cut]
  check,_=make_surface(prefix,'mid_valid',gp)
  for col in ['iv','max_width','prior_ok','shock','guard100','guard50']:
   np.testing.assert_allclose(check[col].to_numpy(dtype=float),relaxed.loc[gp,col].to_numpy(dtype=float),rtol=0,atol=1e-10,equal_nan=True)
  causal={'date':day,'symbol':sym,'cutoff':str(cut),'passed':True}
 return coverage,quality,features,causal
coverage=[];quality=[];features=[];causal=[]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
 tasks=[pool.submit(process,j) for j in jobs]
 for number,task in enumerate(as_completed(tasks),1):
  c,q,f,check=task.result()
  coverage.extend(c);quality.extend(q);features.extend(f)
  if check:causal.append(check)
  if number%50==0:emit('PROGRESS',{'sector_days':number,'total':len(jobs),'elapsed_seconds':round(time.monotonic()-started,1)})
features=pd.DataFrame(features)
expected=pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples([(e.date,e.episode_id,e.parent_min,s,v) for e in parents.itertuples() for s in SYMS for v in VARIANTS],names=['date','episode_id','parent_min','symbol','variant'])
features=features.set_index(list(expected.names)).reindex(expected).reset_index()
for c in ['available','falling','accelerating','quote_change_both_halves']:features[c]=features[c].fillna(False).astype(bool)
features.samples=features.samples.fillna(0).astype(int)
assert len(features)==374*11*4
oldfeatures=pd.read_csv(ROOT/'sector_event_features.csv',float_precision='round_trip')
oldfeatures=oldfeatures[oldfeatures.descriptor.eq('atm')]
check=features[features.variant.eq('original')].merge(oldfeatures,on=['date','episode_id','parent_min','symbol'],validate='one_to_one')
assert check.available_x.eq(check.available_y).all()
np.testing.assert_allclose(check.b1,check.first_half_slope.where(check.available_y),rtol=0,atol=1e-10,equal_nan=True)
np.testing.assert_allclose(check.b2,check.second_half_slope.where(check.available_y),rtol=0,atol=1e-10,equal_nan=True)
np.testing.assert_allclose(check.acceleration_x,check.acceleration_y,rtol=0,atol=1e-10,equal_nan=True)
features['accelerating_with_quote_changes']=features.accelerating&features.quote_change_both_halves
basket=features.groupby(['variant','date','episode_id','parent_min'],sort=True).agg(coverage=('available','sum'),falling_count=('falling','sum'),accelerating_count=('accelerating','sum'),accelerating_with_quote_changes=('accelerating_with_quote_changes','sum')).reset_index()
basket['missing']=11-basket.coverage
for kind in ['falling','accelerating']:
 n=basket[kind+'_count'];basket[kind+'_state']=np.where(n>=6,'yes',np.where(n+basket.missing<6,'no','unknown'))
oldbasket=pd.read_csv(ROOT/'basket_event_features.csv');oldbasket=oldbasket[oldbasket.descriptor.eq('atm')]
bcheck=basket[basket.variant.eq('original')].merge(oldbasket,on=['date','episode_id','parent_min'],validate='one_to_one')
assert bcheck.coverage_x.eq(bcheck.coverage_y).all()
assert bcheck.falling_count.eq(bcheck.n_second_half_falling).all() and bcheck.accelerating_count.eq(bcheck.n_falling_accelerating).all()
emit('FEATURE_FREEZE_BEFORE_OUTCOMES',{'sha256':hashlib.sha256(features.to_csv(index=False).encode()).hexdigest(),'basket_sha256':hashlib.sha256(basket.to_csv(index=False).encode()).hexdigest(),'original_reproduced':True,'causal_checks':causal,'elapsed_seconds':round(time.monotonic()-started,1)})
coverage=pd.DataFrame(coverage)
coverage_summary=coverage.groupby('variant').sum(numeric_only=True).to_dict(orient='index')
for variant in VARIANTS:
 fv=features[features.variant.eq(variant)]
 original=features[features.variant.eq('original')].set_index(['episode_id','symbol'])
 joined=fv.set_index(['episode_id','symbol']).join(original[['available']],rsuffix='_original')
 coverage_summary[variant].update({'valid_sector_windows':int(fv.available.sum()),'recovered_sector_windows':int((joined.available&~joined.available_original).sum()),'lost_original_sector_windows':int((~joined.available&joined.available_original).sum()),'fully_covered_entries':int(basket[basket.variant.eq(variant)].coverage.eq(11).sum())})
emit('COVERAGE',coverage_summary)
emit('COVERAGE_BY_SECTOR',coverage.groupby(['variant','symbol']).sum(numeric_only=True).reset_index().to_dict(orient='records'))
for variant in VARIANTS:
 q=[x for x in quality if x['variant']==variant]
 ds=np.concatenate([x['deviations'] for x in q]);ws=np.concatenate([x['widths'] for x in q])
 totals={k:sum(x[k] for x in q) for k in ['n','missing_bid_iv_nodes','with_neighbors','neighbor_over1','neighbor_over5','prior_ok','unchanged','unchanged_iv_moves']}
 totals.update({'median_neighbor_deviation_pp':np.median(ds) if len(ds) else None,'p95_neighbor_deviation_pp':np.quantile(ds,.95) if len(ds) else None,'median_relative_spread':np.median(ws) if len(ws) else None})
 emit('QUOTE_QUALITY_'+variant,totals)
# Outcome inspection starts only after all variants, coverage and classifications are frozen.
outcomes=pd.read_csv(ROOT/'event_paths.csv',float_precision='round_trip')
assert len(outcomes)==374 and outcomes.episode_id.is_unique
assert outcomes.outcome.value_counts().to_dict()=={'target_first':239,'neither':84,'adverse_first':51}
basket=basket.merge(outcomes[['date','episode_id','parent_min','outcome']],on=['date','episode_id','parent_min'],validate='many_to_one')
groups={'all':outcomes}
for v in VARIANTS:
 b=basket[basket.variant.eq(v)]
 for kind in ['falling','accelerating']:
  for state in ['yes','no','unknown']:groups[v+'_'+kind+'_'+state]=b[b[kind+'_state'].eq(state)]
 for state in ['yes','no','unknown']:groups[v+'_within_falling_acceleration_'+state]=b[b.falling_state.eq('yes')&b.accelerating_state.eq(state)]
old=basket[basket.variant.eq('original')].set_index('episode_id')
for v in VARIANTS[1:]:
 b=basket[basket.variant.eq(v)].set_index('episode_id')
 orig=old.accelerating_state.eq('yes');new=b.accelerating_state.eq('yes')
 for tag,mask in [('retained_original',orig&new),('lost_original',orig&~new),('newly_selected',~orig&new)]:
  groups[v+'_'+tag]=b.loc[mask].reset_index()
 groups[v+'_new_from_unknown']=b.loc[old.accelerating_state.eq('unknown')&new].reset_index()
 groups[v+'_new_from_no']=b.loc[old.accelerating_state.eq('no')&new].reset_index()
def describe(df):
 counts=df.outcome.value_counts()
 return {'n':len(df),'days':df.date.nunique(),'targets':int(counts.get('target_first',0)),'adverse':int(counts.get('adverse_first',0)),'neither':int(counts.get('neither',0)),'hit_rate':float(df.outcome.eq('target_first').mean()) if len(df) else None}
summaries={k:describe(v) for k,v in groups.items()}
assert summaries['original_accelerating_yes']['n']==93 and summaries['original_accelerating_yes']['targets']==67
assert summaries['original_falling_yes']['n']==217 and summaries['original_falling_yes']['targets']==144
emit('OUTCOME_SUMMARIES',summaries)
rng=np.random.default_rng(20260919);draw=rng.integers(0,50,size=(10000,50))
daily={};rates={}
for name,g in groups.items():
 z=g.assign(target=g.outcome.eq('target_first')).groupby('date').agg(n=('episode_id','size'),target=('target','sum')).reindex(dates,fill_value=0)
 a=z[['n','target']].to_numpy(dtype=float);daily[name]=a;total=a[draw].sum(axis=1)
 rates[name]=np.divide(total[:,1],total[:,0],out=np.full(10000,np.nan),where=total[:,0]>0)
contrasts={}

  deletions=[]

   aa=daily[a].sum(axis=0)-daily[a][i];bb=daily[b].sum(axis=0)-daily[b][i]
   if aa[0]>0 and bb[0]>0:deletions.append(aa[1]/aa[0]-bb[1]/bb[0])
  contrasts[a+'__minus__'+b]={'estimate_pp':100*estimate if estimate is not None else None,'interval_pp':(100*np.quantile(diff[finite],[.025,.975])).tolist() if finite.any() else None,'defined_draws':int(finite.sum()),'delete_day_range_pp':[100*min(deletions),100*max(deletions)] if deletions else None}
emit('PAIRED_DATE_BOOTSTRAP',contrasts)
emit('TOY_JAN6_1015',basket[basket.episode_id.eq('2026-01-06_b06_615_1')].to_dict(orient='records'))
emit('QUOTE_UPDATES_DIAGNOSTIC',{v:{'accelerating_selected':int((basket.variant.eq(v)&basket.accelerating_state.eq('yes')).sum()),'selected_with_six_sectors_having_price_changes_in_both_halves':int((basket.variant.eq(v)&basket.accelerating_state.eq('yes')&basket.accelerating_with_quote_changes.ge(6)).sum())} for v in VARIANTS})

import importlib.util,json,math
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
root=Path('outputs/b06_sector_surface_50d_2026-09-13')
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('diagnostic_surface',root/'surface.py')
m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(m)
selected=pd.read_csv(root/'selected_days.csv').date.tolist()
syms=['XLC','XLY','XLP','XLE','XLF','XLV','XLI','XLB','XLRE','XLK','XLU']
jobs=[]
for date in selected:
 for sym in syms:
  path=root/'surfaces'/f'{date}_{sym}.parquet'
  if not path.exists():continue
  z=pd.read_parquet(path,columns=['timestamp','atm','atm_call_status','atm_put_status'])
  s=z.atm_call_status.eq('no_strike_bracket')|z.atm_put_status.eq('no_strike_bracket')
  if s.any():jobs.append((date,sym,z,s))
print('JOBS',len(jobs),'S_MINUTES',sum(int(j[3].sum()) for j in jobs),flush=True)
records=[]; node_records=[]; failures=Counter(); toy=[]
for j,(date,sym,old,s_mask) in enumerate(jobs):
 meta=json.loads((root/'surfaces'/f'{date}_{sym}.json').read_text())
 ivs=[];greeks=[]
 for path in meta['signature']['inputs']:
  d=pd.read_parquet(path)
  (ivs if 'implied_volatility' in path else greeks).append(d)
 p=m._prepare(pd.concat(ivs,ignore_index=True),pd.concat(greeks,ignore_index=True))
 # Relax only bid-IV requirements. Retain positive bid quote, positive midpoint/ask IV,
 # endpoint identity, price ordering, underlying age and original expiry limits.
 numeric=['strike','bid','midpoint','ask','underlying_price','implied_vol','ask_implied_vol']
 relaxed=(np.isfinite(p[numeric])&p[numeric].gt(0)).all(axis=1)
 relaxed &= p.endpoint_match & p.bid.le(p.midpoint)&p.midpoint.le(p.ask)
 relaxed &= p.implied_vol.le(p.ask_implied_vol)
 relaxed &= p.reported_underlying_age_seconds.between(0,60)&p.dte.between(8,65)&p.right.isin(['C','P'])
 assert (~p.valid|relaxed).all()
 p['relaxed']=relaxed
 # Same-contract adjacent observations, with no gap filling or smoothing.
 p=p.sort_values(['expiration','right','strike','timestamp']).reset_index(drop=True)
 contract=p.groupby(['expiration','right','strike'],sort=False)
 for col in ['implied_vol','bid','ask','timestamp']:
  p['prev_'+col]=contract[col].shift(1)
  p['next_'+col]=contract[col].shift(-1)
 previous_one=(p.timestamp-p.prev_timestamp).dt.total_seconds().eq(60)
 next_one=(p.next_timestamp-p.timestamp).dt.total_seconds().eq(60)
 p['has_previous']=previous_one & p.prev_implied_vol.gt(0) & np.isfinite(p.prev_implied_vol)
 p['has_neighbors']=p.has_previous & next_one & p.next_implied_vol.gt(0) & np.isfinite(p.next_implied_vol)
 p['step_iv_pp']=np.where(p.has_previous,100*(p.implied_vol-p.prev_implied_vol).abs(),np.nan)
 p['neighbor_deviation_pp']=np.where(p.has_neighbors,100*(p.implied_vol-(p.prev_implied_vol+p.next_implied_vol)/2).abs(),np.nan)
 p['inside_neighbor_range']=np.where(p.has_neighbors,(p.implied_vol>=p[['prev_implied_vol','next_implied_vol']].min(axis=1))&(p.implied_vol<=p[['prev_implied_vol','next_implied_vol']].max(axis=1)),False)
 p['unchanged_quotes']=p.has_previous&p.bid.eq(p.prev_bid)&p.ask.eq(p.prev_ask)
 p['changed_iv']=p.has_previous&p.implied_vol.ne(p.prev_implied_vol)
 data={c:p[c].to_numpy() for c in p.columns}
 data['valid']=p.relaxed.to_numpy()
 indexes=p.groupby('timestamp',sort=True).indices
 bykey={(str(row.expiration),str(row.right),float(row.strike),row.timestamp):i for i,row in enumerate(p.itertuples())}
 old=old.set_index('timestamp')
 stamps=old.index[(old.atm_call_status.eq('no_strike_bracket')|old.atm_put_status.eq('no_strike_bracket'))]
 recovered=0
 for ts in stamps:
  idx=indexes[ts]; coords=[]; chosen=[]; reasons=[]
  for right in ['C','P']:
   coord,status=m._tenor_coordinate(data,idx[data['right'][idx]==right],None)
   if coord is None:reasons.append(right+':'+status)
   else:
    coords.append(coord)
    for ex in coord['provenance']['expiries']:
     for quote in ex['quotes']:
      chosen.append(bykey[(ex['expiration'],right,quote['strike'],ts)])
  good=len(coords)==2 and coords[0]['underlying']==coords[1]['underlying'] and all(np.isfinite(c['value'][1]) and c['value'][1]>0 for c in coords)
  if not good:
   failures.update(reasons or ['inconsistent_underlying'])
   continue
  recovered+=1
  value=float(np.sqrt((coords[0]['value'][1]**2+coords[1]['value'][1]**2)/2))
  for i in sorted(set(chosen)):
   r=p.iloc[i]
   node_records.append({
    'date':date,'symbol':sym,'time':ts.strftime('%H:%M'),'expiration':r.expiration,'right':r.right,'strike':float(r.strike),
    'bid_iv_missing':not bool(r.valid),'bid_iv':float(r.bid_implied_vol),
    'iv_pp':100*float(r.implied_vol),'previous_iv_pp':100*float(r.prev_implied_vol) if pd.notna(r.prev_implied_vol) else None,
    'next_iv_pp':100*float(r.next_implied_vol) if pd.notna(r.next_implied_vol) else None,
    'bid':float(r.bid),'midpoint':float(r.midpoint),'ask':float(r.ask),'spot':float(r.underlying_price),
    'relative_spread':float((r.ask-r.bid)/r.midpoint),'step_iv_pp':float(r.step_iv_pp),
    'neighbor_deviation_pp':float(r.neighbor_deviation_pp),'has_previous':bool(r.has_previous),
    'has_neighbors':bool(r.has_neighbors),'inside_neighbor_range':bool(r.inside_neighbor_range),
    'unchanged_quotes':bool(r.unchanged_quotes),'changed_iv':bool(r.changed_iv),'iv_error':float(r.iv_error)
   })
  if date=='2026-01-06' and 580<=ts.hour*60+ts.minute<=609:toy.append({'symbol':sym,'time':ts.strftime('%H:%M'),'recovered_atm_iv':value})
 records.append({'symbol':sym,'date':date,'S_minutes':len(stamps),'recovered_minutes':recovered})
 if (j+1)%15==0:print('PROGRESS',j+1,'/',len(jobs),flush=True)
r=pd.DataFrame(records);n=pd.DataFrame(node_records)
print('COVERAGE',r.groupby('symbol')[['S_minutes','recovered_minutes']].sum().to_json(orient='index'),flush=True)
print('COUNTS',json.dumps({'S_minutes':int(r.S_minutes.sum()),'recovered_minutes':int(r.recovered_minutes.sum()),'selected_contract_minutes':len(n),'new_bid_iv_excluded_contract_minutes':int(n.bid_iv_missing.sum()),'candidate_dates':r.date.nunique(),'candidate_sector_days':len(r)}),flush=True)
def summary(x):

 return {'n':len(x),'with_neighbors':len(a),'with_previous':len(b),

 'inside_neighbor_range':int(a.inside_neighbor_range.sum()),
 'relative_spread_quantiles':x.relative_spread.quantile([.5,.9,.95,.99,1]).to_dict(),
 'unchanged_quotes_previous':int(b.unchanged_quotes.sum()),

 'bid_iv_nonfinite':int((~np.isfinite(x.bid_iv)).sum())}
for group,rows in [('bid_iv_excluded',n[n.bid_iv_missing]),('already_accepted_companion_quotes',n[~n.bid_iv_missing])]:
 print('DIAGNOSTICS',group,json.dumps(summary(rows)),flush=True)
print('EXCLUDED_BY_SECTOR',n[n.bid_iv_missing].groupby('symbol').apply(lambda x:pd.Series({'n':len(x),'median_neighbor_deviation_pp':x.neighbor_deviation_pp.median(),'p95_neighbor_deviation_pp':x.neighbor_deviation_pp.quantile(.95),'median_relative_spread':x.relative_spread.median(),'pct_unchanged_quotes':100*x.loc[x.has_previous,'unchanged_quotes'].mean()}),include_groups=False).to_json(orient='index'),flush=True)
cols=['date','symbol','time','expiration','right','strike','previous_iv_pp','iv_pp','next_iv_pp','neighbor_deviation_pp','bid','ask','spot','iv_error']
print('LARGEST_DEVIATIONS',n[n.bid_iv_missing&n.has_neighbors].nlargest(10,'neighbor_deviation_pp')[cols].to_json(orient='records'),flush=True)
print('TOY_RECOVERED',json.dumps(toy),flush=True)
print('UNRECOVERED_FAILURES',dict(failures),flush=True)

1. IV with comparable prices: does the options market tell us something prices haven’t already told us? Imagine two B06 breakouts where the same number of sectors are rising and their typical price gains are almost identical. We paired 73 examples like that, then asked whether the options data separated their outcomes. IV describes how much future movement is priced into options. Our “IV-confirmed” label meant at least six sectors had falling IV, with the slope becoming more negative between the two halves of our lookback. Matching the price conditions helps prevent us from mistaking “prices were already stronger” for “IV supplied useful information.”
Think of three bins for what happened next: rose five points first, fell fifteen points first, or reached neither within the hour. Among the 73 IV-confirmed entries, those bins contained 51, 12 and 10. Among the 73 comparable entries without confirmation, they contained 42, 12 and 19. That is the interesting result: the confirmed group had nine more upward targets and nine fewer unresolved moves. The number of large downward moves was exactly the same. What seems to work is identifying breakouts more likely to produce the initial upward movement we want.
What hasn’t worked is identifying breakouts that are demonstrably safer or more persistent. The twelve adverse outcomes didn’t disappear, and the successful moves weren’t less likely to reverse afterward. Also, these weren’t identical experiments conducted under identical conditions: most matched entries occurred on different dates, and we didn’t equalize every feature of their price paths. Chance or those remaining differences could explain the apparent advantage. The promising claim is “IV may help identify initial progress.” We haven’t established “IV tells us this breakout won’t fail.”
2. Acceleration beyond falling IV: does “falling faster” add anything? Falling and accelerating are different things. Suppose IV moves from 20.0% to 19.9% to 19.6% over equal periods: it fell a little, then fell more. Its decline accelerated. If it moves from 20.0% to 19.7% to 19.6%, it is still falling, but the decline slowed. Our actual calculation compares fitted slopes over two halves of the window. Here we started with entries where IV was already falling broadly, then asked whether requiring the additional acceleration condition improved the result.
There were 217 broadly falling-IV entries. Acceleration qualified in 93, definitely did not qualify in 86, and was unknown in 38. The qualifying group reached the target 72.0% of the time, versus 61.6% for definite nonqualifiers. That looks useful until we ask what the extra restriction throws away. Falling IV alone included 144 successful signals; requiring acceleration retained only 67. We gained a higher observed success percentage while discarding 77 successes. Both facts matter: a higher percentage can come at a very expensive reduction in opportunities.
The extra requirement also didn’t produce stickier winners. Among winners with enough observation time, 28.1% of acceleration qualifiers returned below entry within fifteen subsequent minute closes, versus 15.6% of nonqualifiers. Those differences remain uncertain. There is another complication: qualifiers had a median of eight sectors with falling IV, versus six among nonqualifiers. Some apparent benefit could therefore come from broader IV decline, rather than acceleration itself. Acceleration offers an initial-target hint, but we haven’t shown that the second derivative deserves the credit—or that its benefit justifies excluding more than half the successful opportunities.
3. Useful moves versus brief pops: what does our “win” actually measure? Picture entering SPX at 6,000. It reaches 6,005, so our test records a success. Twenty minutes later it falls to 5,998. The recorded success is still correct: it reached our upward target before the downward boundary. But that record alone says nothing about whether the rally lasted. We had been asking, “Did price reach the first useful destination?” This follow-up asked, “What happened after it got there?”
Among 237 winners with later observations available, 87—36.7%—subsequently closed below their entry price before the original hour ended. However, a winner that reaches its target early has much longer to reverse than one reaching it near the deadline. To make observation time more comparable, we also examined the first fifteen subsequent minute closes, using only winners with all fifteen available. In that check, 49 of 222—22.1%—returned below entry. So a meaningful portion of our successes were moves that later disappeared. The remaining winners weren’t necessarily strong continuing trends; some simply stayed above entry.
The IV condition did not demonstrate protection against those givebacks. That means its higher initial hit rate cannot be translated into confidence that holding longer will work. But a price reversal is also not automatically a failed Branch B trade. If the intended option construction had already completed during the favorable move, the later reversal might be economically irrelevant. The distinction is between getting the movement needed to complete the trade and predicting a sustained rally. Our tests provide evidence about the first price movement; they have not established either sustained momentum or actual option-trade profitability.

# Test 2: does the original IV condition help among comparable price setups?

17 September 2026. Executed after test 1 was saved and independently verified.
**The IV target-rate advantage survives these price controls as a promising but uncertain
association. It still does not reduce adverse outcomes or winner givebacks.**

We found **73 one-to-one pairs, 146 parents**, with exactly the same number of rising
sectors and very similar signed median sector returns. This is a historical comparison
sample; matched membership itself is not an executable entry rule.

| Matched original IV state | Signals / dates / causal advances | +5 first | −15 first | Neither |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Confirmed | 73 / 28 / 39 | 51 = 69.9% | 12 = 16.4% | 10 = 13.7% |
| Definite nonconfirmation | 73 / 27 / 32 | 42 = 57.5% | 12 = 16.4% | 19 = 26.0% |

The target difference is **+12.3 percentage points**, with descriptive whole-date 95%
interval **−3.5 to +27.4**. Adverse difference is exactly zero in this sample, interval
−12.1 to +12.5. The observed separation is nine more targets and nine fewer neither
outcomes, not fewer damaging false starts. Neither difference is −12.3 points, interval
−24.2 to −0.2; this related contrast is exploratory and unadjusted for prior tests.

Original scoring stays +5 SPX points before −15 within sixty minutes from the observed
entry open. Both groups have zero ambiguous cases. A neither is an unresolved price
path within the hour, not necessarily a failed option construction.

![Matched IV comparison and support](/Users/dgrissen/Dev/delta_bomb/outputs/b06_iv_matched_price_2026-09-17/comparison.png)

## What was matched, and what IV means here

This uses the **original** IV condition: at least six of eleven sector ETFs have negative
latest-half ATM IV slope **and** negative acceleration. The existing constant thirty-day
spot-relative ATM measure and T−35…T−6 reference remain unchanged. It is not the later
same-sector price-up/IV-down rule. The full original population remains 93 IV yes,
216 definite IV no and 65 unknown. Unknown is never counted as no.

Price controls use each ETF's full-window endpoint return, 10000×(last/first−1), bps.
Require all eleven ETFs to have complete positive finite thirty-sample price coverage.
Match exactly on count of returns >1e−12 bps. Match the **signed median** return of those
same eleven ETFs within a fixed ten-bps gap (0.10% price return). This is a practical
similarity tolerance fixed before matching, not a validated or optimized threshold.

Matching maximizes pair count first, then minimizes total absolute strength distance,
without replacement. Parent-ID sorting makes tied assignments deterministic. Date, clock
and outcomes do not select pairs. Code/source hashes were frozen before matching; pair
IDs, exclusions and balance diagnostics were frozen before joining original outcomes.

The actual matches are much closer than the allowed gap: **median 0.58 bps, maximum
3.92 bps**, with a mean signed IV-yes minus IV-no gap of −0.15 bps. No wider tolerance
or alternative matching version was tried.

| Price feature | Eligible pre-match IV yes / no means | Matched IV yes / no means | Standardized mean difference, before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Number of rising sectors | 6.63 / 7.07 | 6.70 / 6.70 | −0.179 → 0.000 |
| Median sector return, bps | 4.85 / 8.95 | 5.09 / 5.24 | −0.302 → −0.011 |

Both standardized differences use the same respective **pre-match pooled sample SD**:
2.44 sectors and 13.54 bps. They do not switch scales to flatter the post-match balance.
Each arm has identical counts across rising-sector strata 2…11. The pair and balance
records preserve every actual difference.

## How many comparable entries remain?

The disjoint flow accounts for all 374 parents:

| Step | Parents |
|---|---:|
| Original B06 | 374 |
| Incomplete eleven-sector price coverage, excluded | 97 |
| Complete price coverage remaining | 277 |
| IV unknown within complete price coverage, excluded | 41 |
| Known IV and complete price coverage | 236: 76 yes, 160 no |
| Matched | 146: 73 yes, 73 no |
| Eligible but unmatched | 90: 3 yes, 87 no |

Overall IV unknown is still 65: 24 also lack complete price coverage, so these overlap
with the first exclusion. Among eligible unmatched, seventeen have no counterpart within
the exact-count/caliper rule (two yes, fifteen no); seventy-three have eligible edges but
are unmatched because each counterpart may be used only once (one yes, seventy-two no).

We retained **73/76 = 96.1%** of price-eligible IV-yes observations and **73/93 = 78.5%**
of all IV-yes observations. The matched IV-yes arm contains **51/67 = 76.1%** of the
original IV condition's targets. The twenty original IV-yes parents outside this
comparison contain sixteen targets, one adverse and three neither outcomes. Their
exclusion is a comparability/coverage limitation, not evidence those signals should be
avoided. The full matched sample contains 93 targets out of the original 239; its
confirmed arm contains 51. Do not transfer original full-sample N to this comparison.

## Did the matched winners hold up better?

No clear improvement: among original targets with fifteen subsequent closes available,
**16/48 = 33.3%** of matched IV-yes winners later close below entry, versus
**12/38 = 31.6%** of matched IV-no winners. Difference +1.8 points, interval −16.8 to
+21.1. Three confirmed and four nonconfirmed targets arrive too late for that common
follow-up and remain excluded consistently. This secondary diagnostic preserves the
original winners and does not infer option execution or economic failure.

## What remains uncontrolled

Only **three of the seventy-three pairs share a date**. Median entry time is 12:20 ET
for IV yes and 12:50 ET for IV no. Both arms' three busiest dates supply sixteen entries;
the groups cover different dates and causal advances. Matching does not control time,
advance maturity, leadership identities, dispersion, SPX price path or market regime.
Price snapshots accompany options observations and are not an independent sector feed.

Therefore the finding weakens the simple explanation that IV only picks a higher count
of rising sectors or stronger median returns. It does **not** prove IV is independent
of all price behavior, identify fresh option demand or establish a dealer-hedging mechanism.
The inherited midpoint IV/acceleration signs are not resolved by conservative propagated
quote envelopes; a predictive association and reliably measured repricing are different
claims. No quote uncertainty was reinterpreted as a statistical confidence interval.

## Uncertainty and disposition

Ten thousand identical whole-date draws, seed20260917, retain all fifty sampled dates
including the zero-entry date. Matched membership is fixed; each arm uses its own
resampled denominator. There are no undefined draws. These are **conditional fixed-cohort**
intervals; resampling may disrupt balance, and uncertainty from choosing the match or
matching design is not included. Individual pairs were not treated as independent and
were not rematched after outcomes.

Deleting any one date leaves the target difference positive, **+10.1 to +16.1 points**.
That stability to a single date is useful but does not make the broader interval exclude
zero or create fresh validation. All observations have already been explored, outcomes
overlap, and intervals are unadjusted for the series of hypotheses tried.

**Brent's interpretation:** retain the narrower progress-versus-stalling thesis; no
false-start or durability protection is established. **Research decision:** this is
more encouraging than the participation-change test, and it supplies a concrete matched
sample for inspection. It earns preservation as a candidate association, not a deployed
IV veto or a claim that option-construction accuracy improved. Do not retune matching.
Quant independently verified matching optimality by ordered dynamic programming and
reproduced all labels, exclusions, balance diagnostics, daily cells, intervals and deletions.
No material implementation or report defects were found. Fourteen targeted tests plus
thirty subtests pass, including matching traps, no reuse, missingness and balance scaling.

# B06 test 6: what happens after the original +5 target?

17 September 2026. **A substantial minority of original winners give back the move.
The IV condition's higher initial hit rate does not demonstrate better follow-through.**
All original scores remain unchanged. A later below-entry close is not an option loss:
the intended option construction might already have completed.

## The baseline answer

The same 374 B06 entries produced **239 original targets**, 51 adverse-first outcomes
and 84 neither outcomes, with zero ambiguous cases. Of those 239 targets:

- **87** later have a completed one-minute close below the original entry price.
- **150** have later closes available, but none below entry before the original deadline.
- **Two** reach target in the final minute and have no later close to assess.

Thus **87/237 = 36.7% of assessable winners reverse below entry**. Among those 87,
the first qualifying close occurs a median **ten minute bars after the target bar**,
with middle half six to 24.5 bars and range one to fifty. Some are quick givebacks;
others happen much later. The 150 without an observed reversal are not proven durable
trends: they may stop advancing or give back some of the five points while staying above entry.

The unchanged initial score is **+5 SPX points before −15 within sixty native minute
intervals**, from the original observed entry open. It measures an initial favorable
touch, not lasting momentum, actual option completion or option profitability.

![Post-target givebacks and comparable observation windows](/Users/dgrissen/Dev/delta_bomb/outputs/b06_post_target_2026-09-17/comparison.png)

## Equal observation time: the fifteen-minute check

An early target has much longer to reverse before the original hour ends. The median
target minute starts twelve minutes after entry, leaving **47 subsequent closes**.
Remaining support ranges from zero to 59, with middle half 33–54.

We therefore fixed a separate check before inspecting paths: the **first fifteen later
closes after target**, restricted to winners with all fifteen available before the original
deadline. Fifteen is one quarter of the original hour; it was not selected for its result.

| Existing context | Original target rate | Reversal before original deadline, among assessable targets | Reversal within fifteen later closes, among eligible targets | Targets excluded from fifteen-close check |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All B06 | 239/374 = **63.9%** | 87/237 = **36.7%** | 49/222 = **22.1%** | 17 |
| IV yes | 67/93 = **72.0%** | 26/66 = **39.4%** | 18/64 = **28.1%** | 3 |
| IV no | 132/216 = 61.1% | 47/131 = 35.9% | 24/119 = 20.2% | 13 |

early enough. It does not estimate what would happen to late targets given another
fifteen minutes, nor remove differences in the winners selected by each context. The
short-followed winners are excluded consistently even if they reverse before their deadline.

## Did the improved IV hit rate mean better follow-through?

**There is no demonstrated improvement in that dimension.** IV-positive entries retain
their higher initial target rate, but their observed winner-reversal rates are slightly
higher, both through the original deadline and in the common fifteen-close window.

IV yes minus all B06:

| Descriptor | Difference | Paired whole-date 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original target fraction | +8.1 percentage points | −1.1 to +17.8 |
| Reversal among assessable targets | +2.7 points | −6.6 to +11.0 |
| Reversal within fifteen later closes | +6.1 points | −3.2 to +14.7 |
| Target **and** no observed later reversal / all entries | +2.9 points | −5.3 to +12.0 |

Higher reversal is less favorable for this particular path diagnostic. The last row is
**40/93 = 43.0%** for IV yes versus **150/374 = 40.1%** overall. It counts only targets with
at least one later close and no observed reversal; the zero-follow-up targets do not enter
its numerator. This is a joint descriptive event, **not a replacement win rate**. Its
uncertain advantage is much smaller than the initial +8.1-point target-rate difference.

IV here is the unchanged six-of-eleven falling-and-accelerating ATM condition. Unknown
sector membership stays unknown; this test adds no new surface, threshold or quote filter.

**A versus C:** IV accompanies more initial targets inside broad price participation,
but the winners do not show fewer givebacks. Their full-window reversal difference is
+2.5 points, interval −15.2 to +18.8; the fifteen-close difference is +3.6 points,
interval −11.1 to +18.1. This does not establish lasting follow-through beyond price context.

**B versus D:** IV without broad price participation remains unconvincing. Its fifteen-close

targets. The difference is +27.9 points with interval −4.6 to +63.0; do not promote D as
an inverse signal from these observations.

**B versus C:** the IV-only disagreement group's initial target-rate advantage also does
not establish better persistence. Its fifteen-close reversal difference is +25.2 points,
interval −3.6 to +59.8. Both memberships differ, so this cannot isolate an IV effect.

## Timing rules, uncertainty and limits

For entry minute e and target-touch minute m, inspect closes of bars m+1 through e+59.
The last original bar closes at deadline e+60 and is included; the bar starting at e+60
is excluded. Equality to entry does not count as below (rounding tolerance 1e−8 points).
Wicks alone do not count. The entire target-touch minute is deliberately omitted, as
nominated in the original shortlist. Its final close follows its high, but this
later-minute diagnostic excludes givebacks within that minute. It also misses later
intraminute dips that recover by the close. Lag is measured between minute bars, not
from an invented exact target-touch instant.

All fifty dates, including July 13 with no B06, enter shared 10,000 whole-date draws,
seed 20260917. Every contrast/metric has 10,000 valid draws, and all sixteen intervals
include zero. Delete-date checks retain the IV-versus-baseline reversal differences'
positive direction: +0.6 to +4.1 points over the original window and +3.4 to +7.2 over
fifteen closes. A−C reversal differences can change sign. These are descriptive checks,
not adjusted for earlier research or independent of regime effects. Conditioning on
winners itself changes composition; this is not a causal persistence comparison.

**CIO conclusion:** B06 often supplies the initial movement our score asks for, but a
meaningful fraction of those moves are later given back. IV's observed hit-rate advantage
does not come with demonstrated protection from that giveback. A completed Branch B
construction could still make a later reversal economically irrelevant. Keep the original
winners and this separate path record; add no retrospective entry veto or new exit rule.
